items.title: AI safety filters on Meta, Google models stripped in minutes, FT finds

featured_image.name: Meta to start labeling AI-generated images from companies like OpenAI,  Google - iTnews

items.description: Software tools that remove safety protections from AI models developed by Meta and Google can bypass guardrails in a matter of minutes, according to an investigation published by the Financial Times on Sunday. The modified systems responded to prompts involving biological weapons, malware creation, and child exploitation, raising fresh concerns about the adequacy of voluntary safety measures across the AI industry.

items.title: WHO chief warns Ebola 'outpacing' response as deaths hit 220

featured_image.name: WHO emergency committee meets to discuss Congo Ebola outbreak

items.description:
The World Health Organization's director-general warned on Monday that the Ebola outbreak tearing through the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda is outrunning international containment efforts, with 220 suspected deaths and cases mounting rapidly across the region.

"We are urgently scaling up operations, but at the moment the epidemic is outpacing us," Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, adding that a delay in detecting cases meant responders were now "playing catch-up." He said he would travel to Congo on Tuesday to assess the response firsthand.[1][2]

The remarks came as Uganda confirmed two additional Ebola cases on Monday, bringing its total to seven confirmed infections. The DRC remains the epicenter of the outbreak, with its health ministry reporting hundreds of suspected cases and deaths concentrated in the conflict-ridden Ituri and North Kivu provinces.[1]

items.title: Trump urges Arab leaders to normalize Israel ties as Iran deal nears

featured_image.name: Trump pushes Arab, Muslim leaders on Israel ties

items.description:
President Donald Trump told the leaders of several Arab and Muslim-majority countries during a phone call on Saturday that he expects them to normalize relations with Israel and join the Abraham Accords once a deal to end the war with Iran is reached, according to Axios. The request was reportedly met with silence from the leaders on the call, the Times of Israel reported.[1][2][3]

The call came as Washington and Tehran appeared close to signing a memorandum of understanding to end hostilities, with a senior U.S. official saying the deal could come "in the coming days". Trump declared Saturday that the agreement had been "largely negotiated," though disputes over wording, sanctions relief, frozen assets, and the terms of uranium disposal remain unresolved.[4][5][6]

items.title: Inaudible sounds hidden in podcasts can hijack AI voice assistants, researchers find

items.description: A team of security researchers has shown that imperceptible audio signals hidden in podcasts, YouTube videos, and voice calls can manipulate AI voice assistants into performing unauthorized actions — a finding presented this week at the IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy in San Francisco that exposes a new class of vulnerability in the rapidly expanding world of voice-based AI.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV calls to 'disarm' AI in first encyclical
items.description:
Pope Leo XIV on Monday released his first encyclical, a sweeping nearly 43,000-word document that calls for the "disarming" of artificial intelligence and warns that the technology risks becoming a modern Tower of Babel if left unchecked in the hands of powerful corporations and governments.[1][2]

The encyclical, titled "Magnifica Humanitas" ("Magnificent Humanity"), was presented by the American-born pontiff in the Vatican's Synod Hall — a break with tradition, as popes do not typically speak at the launch of their own encyclicals. Joining him on the panel was Christopher Olah, co-founder of Anthropic, the AI safety company currently embroiled in a legal battle with the Trump administration over the military use of its technology.[3][4]

items.title: Iran says US deal 'not imminent' as both sides temper expectations

featured_image.name: Iran and US agree on 'guiding principles' for a deal, say Iranian officials

items.description:
Efforts to finalize a peace agreement between the United States and Iran slowed on Monday as both sides tempered expectations, with Iran's foreign ministry declaring that a deal is "not imminent" even as Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested an announcement could come "maybe today."

The impasse centers on a proposed memorandum of understanding that would end the three-month-old war, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and set the stage for broader negotiations over Iran's nuclear program and sanctions relief. President Trump, posting on Truth Social over the weekend, said the deal "will either be a great and meaningful one, or there will be no deal," while cautioning his team not to "rush into" an agreement.[1][2]

items.title: Iran agreed to give up enriched uranium in US deal, officials say

featured_image.name: Top Iranian official says Tehran would forgo highly enriched uranium in nuclear  deal with Trump

items.description: Two US officials told the New York Times that Iran has agreed in broad terms to give up its stockpile of highly enriched uranium as part of a framework deal announced by President Donald Trump, who declared Saturday that a peace agreement had been "largely negotiated." But a senior Iranian source subsequently told Reuters that Tehran has not agreed to hand over its enriched uranium, highlighting the persistent contradictions between American and Iranian accounts of the deal's terms.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Trump tells negotiators not to rush Iran deal

featured_image.name: LIVE: Trump instructs negotiators 'not to rush into a deal' with Iran

items.description:
President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he has instructed his negotiators not to "rush into a deal" with Iran, declaring that the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports will "remain in full force and effect" until a final agreement is "reached, certified, and signed."[1][2][3]

The statement came just a day after Trump posted on Truth Social that a memorandum of understanding to end the months-long conflict had been "largely negotiated," raising expectations for an imminent breakthrough.[3][4]
